page: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is a balanced instance in the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 12 shared vCPUs derived from 6 physical Intel x86_64 processor cores operating at a nominal 2.0 GHz clock speed. The server features 48.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache allocations comprise 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and a 16 MB L3 cache pool. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while newer AVX-512 extensions and AMX accelerator units are not present. Local persistence is supplied via a bundled 768 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated GPU acceleration hardware.

Performance testing across standard benchmarks indicates middle-tier execution capabilities across most compute and memory metrics. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1581.0, a multi-core score of 6682.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 17761.33. Single-threaded data compression displayed higher throughput, posting 41.11 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.55 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, alongside a strong PassMark memory benchmark score of 3149.22. However, memory bandwidth across large uncached 256 MB blocks fell into lower comparative tiers at 33.97 GB/sec for reads and 18.41 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, CPU-bound LLM prompt processing for 7B models achieved 22.99 tokens per second, reflecting shared-thread CPU execution constraints on heavy matrix workloads.

From an operational perspective, the instance provides high local storage density with its 768 GB NVMe disk and balanced memory sizing. The primary tradeoff lies in the shared CPU core architecture and modest uncached memory throughput, which makes sustained high-memory bandwidth computations less suitable. Workloads that align well with this configuration include relational databases, cache layers such as Redis (which recorded 13.71 million SET operations per second), static web serving, build and continuous integration pipelines, and routine data transformation jobs.
description: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is a general-purpose virtual server within the High Frequency Compute line, driven by an Intel x86_64 processor delivering 12 shared vCPUs across 6 physical cores at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a bundled 768 GB NVMe SSD for fast local data persistence. Compute benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-tier capabilities, including a PassMark CPU score of 17761.33 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 41.11 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained, measuring 33.97 GB/sec for reads and 18.41 GB/sec for writes. Lacking hardware GPU accelerators, the instance is not geared toward intense machine learning workloads. Its balanced memory, fast storage, and solid multicore performance position it effectively for relational database management, Redis caching tiers, continuous integration pipelines, and static web serving.
